B.oracle: enumerate all torus edge subsets and classify each induced tile pair

C.oracle: enumerate every perfect W-B matching and test strong connectivity directly

D.oracle: enumerate small integer town potentials and check selected person constraints directly

B.proof_equivalent_invariant: Horizontal and vertical edge bits toggle exactly on A cells. Toroidal closure requires even A parity in every row and column. After fixing one base bit per row and column, each B cell is one affine XOR relation between a row and a column base bit; parity-DSU counts solutions.

C.proof_equivalent_invariant: At each cut, p equals the number of backward matching edges crossing that cut. Strong connectivity is equivalent to p>0 at every proper cut; the weighted sweep DP tracks p exactly.
C.constraint_reason: N<=200000 implies on the order of 4e10 DP-state transition opportunities in the frozen implementation.

D.proof_equivalent_invariant: Using town prefix potentials, each person imposes endpoint equality and strict internal inequalities. After contracting equalities, feasibility is exactly acyclicity of the strict-inequality DAG.
D.complexity: Per query rebuilds DSU/graph over N and scans internal vertices of selected intervals.
D.constraint_reason: Q,N up to 2e5 and 4e5; O(QN) initialization alone is about 8e10 operations before interval scans.

x1_reason: No frozen claim-grade correctness failure. C and D are correctness-capable but asymptotically unsafe; X1 cannot be used for a qualitatively new scalable architecture.
